SEO RESOURCING

In-House SEO vs Outsourced SEO Management

Decide whether to manage SEO in-house, outsource it or combine external analysis with internal implementation.

By Cyberfreak Software · 28 November 2026

The right model depends on where work gets stuck

In-house SEO gives a business direct context and control, but requires time, skills and access to useful data. Outsourcing can add specialist capacity, although an external provider still needs input from people who understand the business. Neither model removes the need to make decisions and act on findings.

When in-house ownership works well

An internal marketer or developer may be well placed to make changes quickly, maintain service information and coordinate content. They may still benefit from external review when search data is difficult to interpret or there is no established process for prioritising improvements.

When outsourcing can help

A managed SEO service may be useful when nobody has time to monitor Search Console, maintain the sitemap or turn performance data into a practical task list. Before outsourcing, clarify how recommendations reach the person who can implement them, and how work is approved.

Consider a blended approach

A common arrangement is external monitoring and analysis paired with internal implementation. This keeps business knowledge close to the website while giving the team a regular evidence-based review. It works best when responsibilities and reporting dates are agreed.

A focused external option

Our managed SEO service is designed around Search Console oversight, sitemap maintenance, monthly reporting and keyword/content recommendations. At £125 per month, it does not include content production or substantial development. Those boundaries can make it easier to decide whether your team can take action on the recommendations.
